medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Please refer to the USF Morsani College of Medicine's Student Handbook, beginning on page 38, for the Leave of absence policy. MD Student Handbook, https://documents.health.usf.edu/display/MCOM/MD+Student+Handbook
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The USF Health Morsani College of Medicine is committed to providing an environment rich in activities that promote student wellness and enrich the medical school experience. There are more than 50 medical student organizations, including medical specialty interest groups, social and service organizations, and the BRIDGE Clinic. Information about most organizations is posted on the Student Organizations website: https://health.usf.edu/medicine/mdprogram/student-affairs/student-involvement . These organizations provide excellent opportunities for students to interact socially and professionally with peers and faculty members, as well as patients and others in the community. There are several recreational opportunities for students including a lounge on the medical school campus, access to the university recreation center, athletic playing fields, riverfront park, Channelside, Amelie Arena, Riverwalk, etc.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The MCOM program is located in Tampa. The COM's community training partners include Tampa General Hospital, All Children's Hospital, Moffitt Cancer Center, two large Veterans Affairs hospitals, and various rural clinics.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: USF Health has partnered with Crew Innovations, Inc., to develop Real Estate With Honors, an off-campus listing service to help USF Health students find housing in the Tampa metropolitan area. The free online service accessed at https://health.usf.edu/medicine/mdprogram/housing includes a wide variety of property types, locations, price ranges and sizes such as apartment complexes, houses for sale and/or rent, condos, and even short-term furnished housing. Properties near the USF Health downtown campus and its affiliated clinics and hospitals across the area are represented. Users can inquire about listings and schedule showings through web-based forms and, through internet 3D mapping tools, even have bird's-eye views of each property. The web site includes educational information for first-time buyers and renters, such as off-campus safety and crime prevention articles and a real estate education blog.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Tutoring is available weekdays and weekends.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Our medical students have the opportunity to learn at an extraordinary range of hospitals and teaching centers—among the busiest in the nation.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: The Medical Science Skills Development program is a pre-matriculation program for entering first year medical students who may benefit from a review of the foundational medical sciences.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: Years 1 and 2 of the curriculum are a continuum that introduce students to an organ system-based overview of normal and disease processes, increasing the emphasis on diseases and therapy as the courses progress. Courses integrate anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, cell biology, biochemistry, microbiology and pharmacology relevant to the organ systems under study. Our Core program consists of integrated basic science-clinical experiences, engaged learning, early clinical experience, community outreach programs, and research.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: All students have experiences in primary care sites beginning in year one. All students meet weekly in Year 1-2 with a primary care doctor one-on-one for mentorship and coaching on interviewing and physical diagnosis skills. All students complete an 8 week year 3 interdisciplinary Primary Care Clerkship to work with outpatient physicians in Family Medicine, Pediatrics, Ob-Gyn, and Internal Medicine, seeing and managing common primary care disorders.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: The Scholarly Concentrations Program aims to support the educational development of medical students by providing opportunities for scholarly endeavors in areas of special interest. This program facilitates self-directed learning, enhances interactions between students and encourages relationships between students and faculty. It provides a forum where diversity of ideas and perspectives are valued. Each concentration includes elements of course work, practical application, scholarly presentations and projects allowing for a 4-year scholarly experience.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: The MCOM program's training partners include: Tampa General Hospital, Tampa, FL; All Children's Hospital, St. Petersburg, FL; Moffitt Cancer Center, Tampa, FL; Veterans Affairs hospitals.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: We promise to provide aspiring, passionate students with an open culture of accessibility to faculty, patients, and technology through a challenging curriculum with diverse educational experiences. Transcending old paradigms, the MD program empowers students by offering them a fresh perspective on learning. We foster an environment where students realize their own creativity and innovation to make a difference in the lives of patients and their communities. Upon graduation, our students will possess the skills and confidence as leaders in the ever-changing business of healthcare without ever sacrificing their initial inspiration to care for patients.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The mission of the MD medical education program at the Morsani College of Medicine is to provide for the education of students through the creation of a scholarly environment that fosters excellence in the lifelong goals of education, research activity, and compassionate patient care.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout:
The 7-Year B.S./M.D. Accelerated Program offers First-Time in College (FTIC) USF Judy Genshaft Honors College students the opportunity to receive admission to USF Health’s Morsani College of Medicine (MCOM) and complete a Doctor of Medicine (M.D.) in just seven years — provided that the student continues to meet all program benchmarks, including a successful interview with MCOM.  

Students complete their bachelor’s degree at USF during the first three years, followed by four years at MCOM to earn the M.D. Traditionally, the path to a medical degree takes at least eight years, making this an accelerated track.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Applicants accepted after April 30th have until June 9th to make a final decision.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: A minimum of one letter of recommendation written by a science faculty member.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Interview day will consist of the interview only. Thereafter, interviewees will be invited to participate in online sessions to learn more about the curriculum, meet current medical students, as well as to interact with faculty & staff. Interview opportunities are intended to help the Medical Student Selection Committee reach a decision regarding the appropriateness of USF Health MCOM’s program for your particular needs and goals.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: The MCOM program offers a semi-open file interview format.
medSchoolApplication.secApplName: Anh-Kay Pizano, M.Ed. Assistant Director of MD Admissions
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo: Acceptances are offered  from mid-October to May (of the following year). All admissions decisions are made by the Medical Student Selection Committee and are final. Interviewed candidates are either accepted, waitlisted, or rejected. Once accepted, applicants may submit transcripts from all secondary institutions (Bachelors, Masters, Ph.D., Post-Baccalaureate, etc.). Please ensure that the transcripts are official and final and have your degree conferral date posted.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: USF MCOM views all college coursework taken equally.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Although letters on interest are accepted from all applicants, letters of intent are accepted from applicants on the waitlist only.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: The mission of the Morsani College of Medicine (MCOM) is to educate a diverse group of leaders in medicine and science who will enhance human health through exploration, innovation, scholarship, education, and the provision of the highest quality patient care. Students are expected to develop a robust medical knowledge base and the requisite clinical skills, with the ability to appropriately apply their knowledge and skills, effectively interpret information, and contribute to patient-centered decisions across a broad spectrum of medical situations and settings.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The Financial Aid Office provides guidance throughout the financial aid application process and determines which grant, scholarship, and loan programs the student qualifies for and will best meet their needs. The office also provides debt management and financial planning to all students.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: The tuition and fees for medical students is subject to change each year as established by the Florida State Legislature and the USF Board of Trustees. The Florida State Legislature established procedures for charging tuition and fees to medical and professional students attending Florida State schools on a flat yearly rate basis, regardless of length of time enrolled.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
The USF Morsani College of Medicine - Moffitt Cancer Center MD/PhD Program is designed to foster the development of the next generation of physician-scientists who will make major contributions via translational medicine to enhance the diagnosis and treatment of human disease.

The USF-MCC MD/PhD Program is oriented towards a small group of highly qualified and motivated students and is structured to provide outstanding medical education, scientific training, and state-of-the-art clinical practice by integrating these experiences in an interdisciplinary environment. The program is uniquely tailored to meet the needs of each student, and to promote a deep sense of scientific discovery combined with the application to modern medicine.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Waitlist applicants are evaluated as seats become available and can be offered acceptance up until the first day of classes.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Please review our website regarding the required/recommended premedical coursework at: https://health.usf.edu/medicine/mdprogram/mdadmissions/requirements
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Prerequisite coursework completed more than five (5) years prior will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Applicants are selected for interview based on academic achievement, demonstrated motivation to practice medicine, humanism, leadership, etc. The admissions committee uses a holistic process in reviewing all materials, including interview evaluations, letters of recommendations, course load, and types of courses taken. Applicants from diverse backgrounds, rural communities, and groups unrepresented in medicine are encouraged to apply. Students are encouraged to submit their AMCAS  and secondary applications as soon as possible.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Shadowing mainly includes observation of a physician, including how they spend their day, how they interact and communicate with patients, and how they work with a health care team. This experience allows the student the opportunity to experience a “day in the life” of a health care professional as a way to determine if the career is a personally good fit.
